cool_roof.central_derivation: Hot-arid Phoenix receives weight 2 and Kansas City weight 1: (2*0.66 + 1*0.08)/3 = 0.4667 C.

combination.description: The largest contribution is retained fully; each additional contribution is multiplied by 0.75 to reduce double counting.

entries.study: Street trees provide an opportunity to mitigate urban heat and reduce risk of high heat exposure
entries.effect_relationship: Published observed air-temperature/tree-canopy relationship supports the lower and central tree-cover screening coefficients.
entries.units: degrees C per tree-cover percentage point
entries.notes: Observational association; not a universal causal coefficient.

entries.study: Urban landcover differentially drives day and nighttime air temperature across a semi-arid city
entries.effect_relationship: Published daytime tree-cover coefficient supports the upper tree-cover screening coefficient.
entries.units: degrees C per tree-cover percentage point
entries.notes: Cross-sectional land-cover relationship; used as a screening bound.

entries.study: Scale-dependent interactions between tree canopy cover and impervious surfaces reduce daytime urban heat during summer
entries.effect_relationship: Canopy response is nonlinear and scale dependent.
entries.notes: Supports conservative ranges and extrapolation warnings.

entries.study: Efficacy of cool roofs at reducing pedestrian-level air temperature during projected 21st century heatwaves in Atlanta, Detroit, and Phoenix
entries.climate_context: Hot-arid, humid subtropical, and humid continental
entries.effect_relationship: Extensive cool-roof deployment produced maximum city-averaged daytime cooling of 0.66 C in Phoenix, 0.38 C in Atlanta, and 0.42 C in Detroit.
entries.notes: Phoenix value is assigned stronger relevance for the hot-arid demo; scenario coverage is scaled linearly for MVP screening.

entries.study: Modeling potential air temperature reductions yielded by cool roofs and urban irrigation in the Kansas City Metropolitan Area
entries.effect_relationship: Raising roof albedo by 0.40 produced 0.08 C regional-average daytime cooling under typical summer conditions.
entries.units: degrees C at full modeled deployment
entries.notes: Used as the lower cool-roof evidence point.

entries.study: City of Phoenix Cool Pavement Pilot Program Phase II
entries.effect_relationship: Stationary measurements averaged 0.9 F (0.5 C) cooler over CoolSeal across measured heights and times; the report used 0.55 F (0.306 C) as a widespread-deployment screening estimate and documented some post-sunset reversals.
entries.notes: Mixed hourly signs justify a zero lower bound and explicit uncertainty; policy coverage is scaled linearly for MVP screening.
